sql_schemas: table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups of all leave requests for a given employee; status: filtering by status (SUBMITTED for manager approval queues, APPROVED for calendar views); start_date, end_date: range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; leave_type: filtering by leave type (annual vs sick vs emergency); employee_id, status: combined filter for 'my pending requests' queries

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: lookups of all balances for a given employee; employee_id, fiscal_year: the dominant access pattern — 'my current-year balances'; policy_id: lookups for policy-driven recalculation or bulk accrual jobs; employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year: uniqueness enforcement (one balance row per employee-policy-year)

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: lookup of the active policy for a given leave type; is_active: filtering active policies only

table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup by email; manager_id: lookups for 'my direct reports' queries; employment_status: filtering active employees; department: department-level aggregations

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: lookup of audit trail for a specific entity; performed_by: audit queries by actor; performed_at: time-range audit queries; action: filtering by action type (APPROVE, REJECT, CREATE)

data_notes: Tables defined: leave_requests, leave_balances, leave_policies, employees, audit_logs. The leave_requests table uses leave_type as a string enum (annual, sick, emergency) rather than a FK to leave_policies — this matches the DOMAIN.md spec where LeaveRequest carries leaveTypeId. The leave_balances table links to leave_policies via policy_id. The audit_logs table follows the AuditRecord shape from DOMAIN.md (entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, ip_address, user_agent). All repositories use pg Pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts. The ILeaveRequestRepository.updateStatus and ILeaveBalanceRepository.updateUsedDays accept an optional PoolClient parameter to support caller-controlled transactions.

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted for balance deduction — calendar days (inclusive start..end) or working/business days? Does a half-day leave consume 0.5 or 1 day?
open_questions.impact: Affects the day-count computation used when deducting from leave_balances.used_days on approval. Every query that sums used days for a period (countByEmployeeAndTypeInPeriod, balance updates) must use the same counting rule.
candidate_options: Business days: exclude weekends + public holidays (requires holiday calendar)
Half-day support: start_date and end_date may include a half-day flag

open_questions.question: What defines the fiscal_year boundary for leave balances — calendar year, a configurable fiscal year (e.g. Apr–Mar), or employee hire-date anniversary?
open_questions.impact: Determines which balance row is used when approving a leave request that spans a boundary, and how the fiscal_year value is computed in leave_balances queries.
candidate_options: Custom fiscal year: e.g. Apr 1 – Mar 31 (configurable per tenant)

transaction_contract: Multi-step writes that must be atomic (e.g. approving a leave request: update leave_requests.status + update leave_balances.used_days/remaining_days) use a caller-controlled transaction pattern. Repository methods that may join a caller's transaction (updateStatus on ILeaveRequestRepository, updateUsedDays on ILeaveBalanceRepository) accept an optional PoolClient parameter. When omitted, the method acquires its own connection from the shared pool for the single operation. The calling service owns the unit of work: it acquires a client from the pool, executes BEGIN, passes the client to each participating repository method, then executes COMMIT or ROLLBACK. The service must release the client back to the pool in a finally block.
